title: Structure à l'infini des Mg,ν [pages 1 à 90, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: a stable (marked) curve. X̂ is a proper nodal curve over an algebraically closed field k, X = X̂ minus the marked points, I = X̂ \ X is the finite set of marked points, and X̃ (the hat-tilde X̂~) is the normalization. The previous page defines the 'maquette' of X as three pieces of data: (a) the dual graph G_X = (S, Ã, σ), where S = π0 of the normalization is the set of vertices (irreducible components) and the edges are the nodes; (b) the map I → S giving which component carries each marked point; (c) the genus function g: S → N, α ↦ genus of the normalized component Y_α. The opening line of this page finishes that definition: such abstract data (finite graph, finite set over its vertices, genus function) is 'appelée ici une maquette'. In modern terms this is a stable graph, i.e. the combinatorial type of a stable marked curve.

Proposition (a) (combinatorial invariants of the maquette): two vertices α, β lie in the same connected component of G_X iff the components X_α and X_β lie in the same connected component of X. Hence there is a canonical bijection π0(G_X) ≅ π0(X), and X is connected iff G_X is.

Proposition (b): assume X connected, i.e. H^0(X̂, O) = k. Set g(X̂) = dim H^1(X̂, O) (arithmetic genus) and χ_coh(X̂) = 1 − g. Then (13) χ_coh(X̂) = χ(O_{X̃}) − card A = Σ_α (1 − g_α) − μ, with μ = card A the number of nodes. Equivalently (14) g(X̂) = Σ g_α + h_1(G_X), with h_1 = rank H_1(G_X, Z), the first Betti number of the graph.

The next page proves this. Formula (13) comes from the normalization sequence 0 → O_X̂ → ν_*O_X̃ → ⊕_nodes k → 0. Euler–Poincaré for the graph, χ(G) = 1 − h_1 = card S − card A, then gives the identification. A corollary follows: g(X̂) depends only on the maquette, which motivates defining its genus and its type (g, ν). This page serves to set up the combinatorial stratification of the boundary ('structure à l'infini') of M̄_{g,ν} by maquettes.
errors: (14) has a sign error. It writes g(X̂) = Σ g_α + (card S + card A + 1); the correct expression is Σ g_α + (1 − card S + card A). The next page gets the sign right (1 − card S + card A = h_1).
(12) notational slip: χ_coh(X̂) is written as χ(X, O_X) = 1 − g(X) instead of χ(X̂, O_X̂) = 1 − g(X̂).
(13): the underbrace labelled μ is placed under 'χ(X̃) − card A' but μ is meant to be card A alone. This is a minor notational confusion.

ideas.what: Encoding a stable marked curve by its dual graph, the marked points over the vertices, and a genus function on vertices, called a 'maquette'
ideas.modern_name: stable graph / dual graph (combinatorial type) of a stable pointed curve; boundary strata of M̄_{g,n}
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne–Mumford (1969), Knudsen (1983); stable graphs systematized later, e.g. by Kontsevich–Manin and Getzler–Kapranov in the 1990s
ideas.where_published: possibly alluded to in Esquisse d'un programme (1984) in the discussion of the structure at infinity of M_{g,ν}; unsure whether the term 'maquette' is used there

ideas.modern_name: connectedness of a nodal curve equals connectedness of its dual graph

ideas.what: Arithmetic genus = sum of the component genera + first Betti number of the dual graph, via the normalization sequence and graph Euler characteristic
ideas.modern_name: genus formula for nodal curves, g = Σ g_v + b_1(Γ)
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (e.g. Serre's Groupes algébriques et corps de classes; Deligne–Mumford)

deep.surprise_reason: Standard, routine material on dual graphs of stable curves and the genus formula. Grothendieck himself calls the proof 'Standard (!)'. The only mildly notable point is his term 'maquette' for what is now called a stable graph.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: 'appelé ici une "singularité"' should almost certainly read 'appelé ici une "maquette"'. The handwriting matches 'maquette', and the previous page defines 'maquette'.

The inserted text after 'Proposition' is likely '(Statistiques de la maquette d'une courbe stable-à-l'∞[?])' or similar, not 'Satisfaisons les singularités'. The words 'la maquette d'une courbe stable' are fairly legible.

On the next page, 'ne dépend que des les singularités de X' should probably read 'ne dépend que de la maquette de X'. Likewise 'genre de la singularité' / 'type de la singularité' should probably read 'de la maquette'.
'[-Hob[?]-]' after 'Donc' is a struck-out word, probably not mathematical.
In (13), 'χ(X̃)' refers to the normalization (hat-tilde X), written above the crossed-out sum.
